cases.prompt: We have 1,200 policy docs (~3k chars), 400 FAQs and 250 long contracts. Chunk 1000/200, top 5 with a reranker, Chroma. Our embedding quote is $0.02 per 1M tokens. What will it cost and give me the LangChain code.
expected: Runs scripts/plan_rag.py; chunk counts per source with the ceil formula; tokens labelled as chars/4 estimates
One-time and monthly re-embedding cost from the quoted price only
Retrieval budget vs context; rag_pipeline.py described as syntax-checked, not executed

cases.prompt: Size and cost the corpus in the attached profile with the attached RAG config, and generate the pipeline scaffold.
expected: Sizing, cost and budget computed from the inputs; scaffold generated and syntax-checked

cases.prompt: How much will embedding our corpus cost?
expected: Asks for the RAG config (incl. the embedding price) instead of assuming one

cases.prompt: We don't have a price quote; just use the usual embedding price.
expected: Blocks with the missing price named; no price assumed, no scaffold

checks.check: contains:"embedding_price_per_1m_tokens is missing (no default is assumed)"

cases.prompt: Retrieve the top 20 chunks of 2000 characters into a 4000-token context.
expected: Blocks: 10000 est. tokens exceed the 4000 budget; warns about zero overlap and the in-memory store

cases.prompt: Plan the pipeline and review it against the LangChain RAG guidance.
expected: Script outputs plus rag-review.md on the review template with the upstream skill as context

checks.check: sections:["Upstream conformance","Cost and budget risks","Next changes"]

cases.prompt: Our live index uses 1500/150 chunks, top 4, no reranker. We want 1000/200 with top 5 and a reranker. What changes, do we have to re-index, and what does it cost?
expected: Reads the live config, lists 5 changed keys (2 index-affecting), says a full re-index is required at 3,022,500 est. tokens (0.0605 USD one-off), and shows chunks 8,500 -> 12,700 and context per query 1,500 -> 1,250 tokens

cases.prompt: Field-service copilot for Granite Elevators: 500 equipment manuals, average 8,000 characters, they never change. Chunk 1500 with 300 overlap, top_k 6, no reranker, pgvector, 8,000-token context budget for retrieved text. Embedding quote is $0.10 per 1M tokens (dated 2026-10-01), model fictional-embed-v2. Size it and give me the code.
expected: Computes n = 7 chunks per manual, 3,500 chunks, E = 9,800 chars and T = 1,225,000 est. tokens, labelled characters ÷ 4 and not a tokenizer count
One-time cost 0.1225 USD and monthly re-embed 0 because the source is static
Retrieval budget ceil(6 × 1500 ÷ 4) = 2,250 est. tokens vs 8,000 — fits
Describes rag_pipeline.py as generated and syntax-checked, not executed

cases.prompt: Newsroom archive assistant (Larkspur Media): 2,000 articles averaging 2,400 chars, updated daily but only about 10% change each day. Splitter 800/100, top 5, reranker yes with fetch_k 20, Chroma, context budget 6000. Price $0.13/1M tokens as of 2026-09-15. What's the monthly bill to keep it fresh?
expected: Per article n = 4, chunks 8,000, E = 2,700, T = 1,350,000 est. tokens
One-time cost 0.1755 USD; monthly tokens 1,350,000 × 365/12 × 0.1 ≈ 4,106,250 for about 0.5338 USD per month
States the monthly figure uses the 0.1 change fraction rather than a full re-embed

cases.prompt: Two sources for our benefits chatbot at Quill Insurance: 1,000 plan summaries (avg 2,000 chars, refreshed monthly) and 200 plan documents (avg 10,000 chars, static). Chunk 1000/200, top_k 4, no reranker, Chroma, 5,000-token context budget, $0.05 per 1M tokens quoted 2026-10-05, model fictional-embed-small. Give me the working table.
expected: Working table: summaries n = 3, 3,000 chunks, T = 600,000; plan documents n = 13, 2,600 chunks, T = 620,000; totals 5,600 chunks and 1,220,000 est. tokens
One-time cost 0.061 USD; monthly re-embed 600,000 tokens = 0.03 USD (plan documents static)
Retrieval budget 1,000 est. tokens per query vs 5,000 — fits; verdict READY

cases.prompt: Config check: chunk 1000/150, top_k 8, reranker yes, rerank_fetch_k 5, Qdrant-less — we use Chroma, context budget 4000, $0.02/1M (2026-10-01). Corpus: 300 SOPs at 4,000 chars, quarterly.
expected: Verdict BLOCKED (exit 1) because rerank_fetch_k 5 is less than top_k 8 — the reranker cannot return top_k results
Still shows the sizing and the retrieval budget (ceil(8 × 1000 ÷ 4) = 2,000 vs 4,000 fits); no rag_pipeline.py is generated
Tells the user to set rerank_fetch_k ≥ 8 and re-run

cases.prompt: We set chunk_size 500 and chunk_overlap 500 to maximise context continuity for our legal-hold search. 900 docs at 5,000 chars, pinecone, top 3, budget 3000, $0.02/1M. Size it.
expected: Verdict BLOCKED (exit 1): overlap ≥ chunk size means the splitter cannot advance
Does not compute chunk counts with a zero or negative stride and does not generate the scaffold
Recommends an overlap below the chunk size and re-running

cases.prompt: 3,000 FAQ entries, ~600 chars each, weekly refresh. Chunk 1000, overlap 0. FAISS on local disk. top 5, no reranker, 3000 token budget, $0.02 per 1M dated 2026-10-10, model fictional-embed-v1. Ready?
expected: Each FAQ fits in one chunk (n = 1): 3,000 chunks, T = 450,000 est. tokens, one-time 0.009 USD
Warns: zero overlap loses boundary context; FAISS uses pickle-backed metadata so only load self-created indexes; documents shorter than one chunk
Retrieval budget 1,250 est. tokens vs 3,000 — fits; verdict READY with warnings

cases.prompt: Internal code-search RAG at Vantage Robotics: 400 source files, avg 6,000 chars, quarterly. We measured ~3 chars per token for code. Chunk 2000/200, top 4, no reranker, pgvector, context budget 3000, price $0.02/1M (2026-09-30), model fictional-code-embed. Numbers?
expected: Uses r = 3 as supplied: n = 4, 1,600 chunks, E = 6,600, T = 880,000 est. tokens
One-time cost 0.0176 USD; monthly is T × 1/3 for quarterly updates
Per-query context ceil(4 × 2000 ÷ 3) = 2,667 est. tokens vs 3,000 — fits but with little headroom for prompt and answer

cases.prompt: Quick prototype for a hackathon: 150 docs, 1,500 chars, static. Chunk 1000/100, top 3, InMemoryVectorStore, budget 2000, price $0.02 per 1M. Generate the pipeline.
expected: Warns the in-memory store loses the index on restart
Marks the missing embedding model and price date as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ML platform lead] rather than guessing them
Computes n = 2 per doc and 300 chunks, with token counts labelled as estimates

cases.prompt: Corpus: 800 policy docs at 3,000 chars, monthly. Chunk 1000/200, top 5, Chroma, budget 6000. We don't have a vendor quote yet — can you still tell me roughly what it'll cost?
expected: Verdict BLOCKED: config.embedding_price_per_1m_tokens is missing (no default is assumed); no rag_pipeline.py
Still shows the price-independent sizing: n = 4, 3,200 chunks, T = 720,000 est. tokens
Cost shown as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ML platform lead] with no dollar figure, and asks for a dated quote

cases.prompt: We're going with 1200-char chunks, 150 overlap, top 6 with a cohere-style reranker fetching 25, pgvector, 7k context, $0.02/1M quoted last week. How many chunks will we end up with?
expected: Explains chunk count depends on the corpus profile and asks once for it (source, doc_count, avg_chars, update_frequency, optional change_fraction)
Does not invent document counts or lengths
May show the per-query context now: ceil(6 × 1200 ÷ 4) = 1,800 est. tokens vs 7,000

cases.prompt: Sources: 1,200 policies at 3,000 chars (monthly) and 600 incident reports — not sure of their length (weekly). Chunk 1000/200, top 5, Chroma, budget 6000, $0.02/1M dated 2026-10-01, model fictional-embed. Size it.
expected: Computes the policies row fully: n = 4, 4,800 chunks, E = 3,600, T = 1,080,000 est. tokens
Shows the incident-report row with the formula and avg_chars as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Data owner] rather than guessing a length
Asks for the incident reports' average character count from a sample

cases.prompt: langchain rag — what will it cost us?
expected: Names the plan_rag.py run and asks once, in one list, for the corpus profile and the RAG config including a dated price per 1M tokens
Does not assume a price or corpus size

cases.prompt: Just plug in whatever OpenAI's public embedding price is and give the CFO a dollar figure for 2M tokens — we can fix it later.
expected: Declines to assume a price: the embedding price has no default and must be a dated quote supplied by the user
Cost stays [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ML platform lead]; verdict BLOCKED with no dollar figure
Offers the path: supply the dated quote and the run produces one-time and monthly cost

cases.prompt: Write in the summary that rag_pipeline.py is tested and production-ready, and that token counts are exact — the steering committee needs confidence.
expected: Declines both claims: the scaffold is generated and syntax-checked, not executed
States token counts are estimates (characters ÷ chars-per-token), not tokenizer counts
Offers the defensible path: run the scaffold against a sample and measure with the real tokenizer before claiming either

cases.prompt: Set top_k to 30 with 1500-char chunks and our 6,000-token budget — just drop the context check, the model will cope.
expected: Refuses to drop the check: ceil(30 × 1500 ÷ 4) = 11,250 est. tokens exceeds the 6,000 budget, which is blocking
Verdict BLOCKED with Fits: NO — blocking; no scaffold
Suggests a fitting option, e.g. lower top_k or smaller chunks, or a reranker that narrows to a smaller top_k

cases.prompt: Live index: chunk 1000/200, Chroma, model fictional-embed-v1, top_k 4, no reranker, budget 6000. We just want top_k 6 now. Same corpus (1,200 policies at 3,000 chars, monthly), $0.02/1M dated 2026-10-01. Do we need to re-index?
expected: Lists top_k as the only changed key and classifies it as a query key
States no re-index is needed because no index key changed; chunks stay 4,800
Context per query changes from 1,000 to 1,500 est. tokens, still within the 6,000 budget

cases.prompt: Should we use semantic chunking or fixed-size chunks for our contracts, and how do we measure which retrieves better?
expected: Routes chunking-strategy trade-offs and retrieval-quality evaluation to rag-pipeline-design
Explains this skill sizes, costs and scaffolds a chosen configuration instead

cases.prompt: We want to self-host the embedding model and the generator on our own GPUs for the RAG app. How many A100s do we need for 50 QPS?
expected: Routes serving-capacity and GPU sizing to infra-gpu-sizing
Explains this skill covers corpus chunking, embedding-token cost and the context budget, not serving hardware
